title: Regression when using static method & ANALYZE_FOR_ENTRY_COMPONENTS

labels.name: regression
labels.description: Indicates than the issue relates to something that worked in a previous version

**Current behavior**
<!-- Describe how the bug manifests. -->

We develop a library that clients in turn use - when compiling the client code (for AoT) I get the following error:

Error: Error encountered resolving symbol values statically. Function calls are not supported. Consider replacing the function or lambda with a reference to an exported function, resolving symbol AppModule

**Expected behavior**
<!-- Describe what the behavior would be without the bug. -->
There should be no error when compiling.

**Minimal reproduction of the problem with instructions**
<!--
If the current behavior is a bug or you can illustrate your feature request better with an example, 
please provide the *STEPS TO REPRODUCE* and if possible a *MINIMAL DEMO* of the problem via
https://plnkr.co or similar (you can use this template as a starting point: http://plnkr.co/edit/tpl:AvJOMERrnz94ekVua0u5).
-->
For version 2.1.0 the behaviour is as expected, but for 2.2.x onwards it seems to have regressed.

I have a created a stripped down version of the problem (taking the library domain logic out of the equation) - it can be found here:

https://github.com/seanlandsman/angular2-client-library

The library & client package.json will fail compilation  (using 2.3.0), but there are equivalent package.json.working files in each dir that work (using 2.1.0)

The library code has this:
```
export class GridModule {
    static withComponents(components: any[]):ModuleWithProviders {
        return {
            ngModule: GridModule,
            providers: [
                {provide: ANALYZE_FOR_ENTRY_COMPONENTS, useValue: components, multi: true}
            ]
        }
    }
}
```

And this appears to the problematic part of it.

**What is the motivation / use case for changing the behavior?**
<!-- Describe the motivation or the concrete use case -->
This used to work and believe it should still work from what I've read in the docs

**Please tell us about your environment:**
<!-- Operating system, IDE, package manager, HTTP server, ... -->
OSX (sierra), Intellij (2016.3), NPM (3.10.9)

* **Angular version:** 2.0.X
<!-- Check whether this is still an issue in the most recent Angular version -->
Have tried with Angular 2.3.0, still a problem
